assumptions: Natural isotope abundances, convolved per element, as an instrument that does not resolve fine structure sees it.
limits: Coarse: isotopic fine structure is deliberately not resolved.
No instrument response, resolution or detector saturation.
bio.jane/contract.question: What coarse isotope pattern does this peptide or formula show: the heights and masses of M, M+1, M+2 and beyond?

description: Coarse isotope pattern of a peptide or of an elemental formula (C29H31N7O, as a compound's formula reads): the relative heights and masses of its M, M+1, M+2 … peaks as an instrument that does not resolve isotopic fine structure sees them, computed by per-element convolution from natural abundances (validated against OpenMS).

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

charge.description: protons added; masses then include them (divide by the charge for m/z).

formula.description: elemental formula of a neutral compound (C29H31N7O; isotopes as C[13]); give this or `sequence`.

maxIsotope.description: peaks to keep (M counts as one); 0 keeps every peak.

sequence.description: peptide, plain one-letter residues; give this or `formula`.

name: isotope_envelope

peaks.description: one row per peak: isotope index, mass, relative abundance (sums to 1)
